title: Heat an ideal emitter
hook: Change absolute temperature and predict radiated power.
misconception: radiated power doubles when absolute temperature doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply P = σAT⁴ to compare radiated power when absolute temperature changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With an ideal blackbody of fixed area ignoring incoming radiation, P = σAT⁴. When absolute temperature doubles, radiated power becomes 16 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model P = σAT⁴; scaling exponent 4. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider an ideal blackbody of fixed area ignoring incoming radiation, with a nonzero initial result. If absolute temperature triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on radiated power?
recall.why: Apply P = σAT⁴ under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 81.
